record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: For every logconcave density f on R^n with covariance matrix A_f, is the isoperimetric coefficient Φ_f always bounded below by an absolute constant times 1/sqrt(λ_1(A_f)), where λ_1(A_f) is the largest eigenvalue of A_f? That is, does there exist an absolute constant c such that Φ_f ≥ c / sqrt(λ_1(A_f)) for all logconcave densities?

evidence.quote:
I Conjecture 19 (KLS). Let f be a logconcave density in R^n. There is an absolute constant c such that
Φ_f ≥ c / sqrt(λ_1(A_f)).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to[0,\infty)$ be a logconcave probability density, i.e., $\log f$ is concave on its support and $\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f=1$. Let $A_f$ denote the covariance matrix of $f$, with largest eigenvalue $\lambda_1(A_f)$. Define the isoperimetric (Cheeger) coefficient of $f$ by
$$\Phi_f \;=\; \inf_{S\subset\mathbb{R}^n}\; \frac{\int_{\partial S} f\,d\sigma}{\min\!\left(\int_S f,\;\int_{\mathbb{R}^n\setminus S} f\right)},$$
where the infimum is over all measurable subsets $S$ with sufficiently regular boundary (and $\int_{\partial S} f\,d\sigma$ denotes the boundary measure induced by $f$).

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant $c>0$, independent of the dimension $n$ and of $f$, such that for every logconcave probability density $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\Phi_f \;\geq\; \frac{c}{\sqrt{\lambda_1(A_f)}}\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The full KLS (Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits) conjecture in this form remains open as of 2025. Major progress has been achieved: Chen (2021) gave a near-constant bound, Klartag–Lehec (2022) reduced the gap to polylog factors, and in late 2024 Klartag and Lehec (using a technique of Guan) resolved the related Bourgain slicing conjecture and the thin-shell conjecture, which yield the current best polylogarithmic bounds for KLS. However, an absolute (dimension-free) constant $c$ has not been established.

status_evidence.snippet: Bourgain's slicing problem was resolved in December 2024 by Klartag and Lehec; KLS implies slicing but not conversely.
status_evidence.claim: Related conjectures resolved, but KLS itself remains open.

status_evidence.title: Bourgain's slicing problem and KLS isoperimetry up to polylog
status_evidence.snippet: Klartag–Lehec establish KLS isoperimetry up to polylogarithmic factors.
status_evidence.claim: Best known bound on KLS is up to polylog, not an absolute constant.
